small_guidance:
- Drop atomic_max: it serializes writes across N-tiles. Make BLOCK_N span the full N (N=8192/POOL=512 fits) or split-N with a separate reduction kernel; one program per row (or row-tile) computes full pooled vector, applies GELU+scale, and reduces to scalar with tl.max in registers.
- With M=1024, N=8192, K=8192, try a row-persistent design: BLOCK_M=32 or 64, BLOCK_N=512–1024 (whole pooled row in one program), loop over K with BLOCK_K=64–128, num_warps=8, num_stages=3–4. Pre-transpose W once (already done) — good.
- Add more autotune configs with smaller BLOCK_M (16/32) and very large BLOCK_N (256/512) since M=1024 is small relative to N; also try GROUP_M=4.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as "one program per output row (or small row-tile)" that streams the full K dimension and accumulates the entire N=8192 output into registers/shared memory in pooled form (BLOCK_N tile loops, accumulating pooled buckets directly to avoid storing full 8192 logits). Then fuse bias+GELU+scale+max as a pure in-register epilogue with no atomics.
- Alternatively, two-kernel pipeline: (1) tiled GEMM writing pooled+gelu+scaled output of shape (M, N/POOL_K) to global memory; (2) tiny row-reduction kernel for max. This removes atomic_max contention and lets each kernel autotune independently.
- Consider fp16/bf16 tensor-core inputs (cast x and W to bf16, accumulate fp32) for ~2× GEMM throughput on Ada; the reference is fp32 but tolerance 5e-2 easily accommodates bf16 matmul. Keep epilogue in fp32.
